intended_application: food packaging; suggested as paper coatings for dry foods such as nuts or legumes

process_steps.description: Orange residue (peel and pulp) scalded to deactivate enzymes

source.quote: the residues (peel and pulp) were scalded to deactivate the endogenous enzymes
freeze-dried at −50 °C under vacuum (30 Pa)
ground, and sieved (<0.08 mm)

process_steps.description: Orange residue added to citric acid solution at pH 1.5, solid:liquid 5:300

source.quote: the orange residue was poured into a citric acid solution (10% w/v with an adjusted pH of 1.5) respecting a solid:liquid ratio of 5:300

process_steps.description: Extraction at 25 °C with 142 W/L acoustic energy, for 30 min

source.quote: The temperature during the extraction was maintained at 25 ± 2 °C with a thermostatic bath by driving a refrigerant liquid (ethylene glycol) through the double-jacketed vessel where the extraction was carried out. The amount of acoustic energy applied was assessed with the calorimetric method [28] and was found to be 142 ± 5 W/L. The extraction was carried out for 30 min
the mix was centrifugated (20 min at 4000 rpm) and filtrated

process_steps.description: Pectin precipitated with twice the volume of ethanol and stirred

source.quote: the liquid was treated with twice the volume of ethanol (96% v/v) and stirred for 10 min

process_steps.description: Centrifuged and filtered again; precipitate washed with ethanol and acetone

source.quote: The mixture was centrifugated again (20 min at 4000 rpm) and filtrated, and the precipitated material was washed with absolute ethanol and acetone

process_steps.description: Semi-pure pectin dried under vacuum overnight, ground and sieved below 0.355 mm

source.quote: The extracts were dried in an oven at 40 °C under vacuum overnight, ground, and sieved (<0.355 mm)

process_steps.description: Semi-pure pectin dissolved at 2% w/w with stirring at 500 rpm

source.quote: Aqueous solutions at 2% w/w of CP and SP pectic materials were prepared by keeping them under agitation for 24 h at 500 rpm

process_steps.description: Chitosan solution added to the pectic solution

source.quote: 0.4 g of either component was added to 100 g of each pectic solution

process_steps.description: Homogenised with a rotor–stator homogenizer at 10,000 rpm

source.quote: The mixtures were then homogenized using a rotor–stator homogenizer (Polytron 3100D, Mississauga, ON, Canada) for 5 min at 10,000 rpm
underwent ultrasound treatment for 1 min (60% amplitude)
the solutions were drop-casted into circular Teflon molds of 100 mm in diameter

process_steps.description: Dried at room temperature under a fume hood

source.quote: The films were dried for about 72 h at room temperature under a fume hood

recipes.description: Semi-pure pectin extracted from orange residue with citric acid, with chitosan added at 20% w/w of the pectic film

source.quote: Aqueous solutions at 2% w/w of CP and SP pectic materials were prepared by keeping them under agitation for 24 h at 500 rpm
0.4 g of either component was added to 100 g of each pectic solution
chitosan solution (1% w/w chitosan in 2% w/w acetic acid aqueous solution)

properties.name: oxygen_permeability
properties.test_details: manometric method, dry oxygen, films purged with N2 for 15 h

source.quote: O2 permeation of this film (SP_Chi) is in the same order of magnitude as the permeation of its two components at 4.37 × 10−19 m3·m/Pa·m2·s

best_recipes.criterion: default: main orange-residue formulation; chitosan improved water resistance and strength while keeping the oxygen barrier

source.quote: Chitosan improved the water resistance and strength in SP films while maintaining high oxygen barrier properties
